To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a unified description of the inclusive and diffractive structure function data at HERA in the dipole approach with a saturation scale ${\ensuremath{Q}}_{s}$ larger than 1GeV for x=10-5 and that the description includes heavy quarks and a $q\overlin{q}g\ensuremath{\rightarrow}q\overlin{\mathrm{q}}g$ final state in the dipole amplitude.
the dipole picture of diffractive DIS, with a saturation model fitted to inclusive DIS data, describes HERA data on diffractive DIS with a ${\ensuremath{χ}}^{2}$ per point of 1.2.
we provide the first parameter-free description of HERA diffractive data in a unified framework with saturation, and that the saturation scale ${Q}_s$ is larger than 1 GeV at $x=10^{-5}$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of the strong interaction in a regime where the coupling of QCD is strong.
the development of a unified description of inclusive and diffractive deep-inelastic scattering in the saturation regime.
the study of the structure of hadrons in the framework of the dipole picture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dipole picture provides a unified description of the inclusive and exclusive structure functions in deep inelastic lepton-hadron scattering.
, in the kinematical range where the HERA diffractive data have been collected and where they are compared to the predictions of the model, the latter is in good agreement with the former.
we have a model which describes the data well and has the right features to be a model of saturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dipole picture with the saturation model can describe inclusive deep inelastic structure functions and diffractive deep-inelastic scattering data with a single parameter set.
the dipole picture is a very useful tool for the description of inclusive and diffractive deep-inelastic scattering data.
the dipole model, which is based on perturbative QCD and is successful in describing the inclusive structure functions, can also be applied to the diffractively scattered protons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the saturation scale is large enough to describe the HERA data.
saturation effects are relevant in the kinematic region of the HERA diffractive data.
saturation is a necessary ingredient in a unified description of inclusive and diffractive deep-inelastic scattering.
